title: The pull requests read beside a repository
description: Everything a reading discovers about the pull requests fetched beside a working tree: the words each one's changed files write above both references, what its own description says beside what it changes, the work it states and writes, and what published vocabularies call its words. It is a document of its own because it answers a different question about a different corpus, so the repository's own figures cannot move when this shape does.

schemaVersion.title: Schema version
schemaVersion.description: The version of this document's shape. It rises when a field is added, renamed or removed. Consuming code branches on it.

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: The repository these pull requests are of, as the host names it — owner/name. Empty where the fetch step recorded none.

pullRequests.title: Pull requests read
pullRequests.description: One entry per pull request read beside the working tree, each read as its own tree: the changed files at its head commit, scored against thresholds its own permutation null sets. The blocks above are the working tree's alone, so one document reads the repository with these pull requests and without them. Empty where none was read.

number.title: Number
number.description: The pull request number its repository states.

author.title: Author
author.description: The author the pull request was selected by, as the host states the login.

headSha.title: Head commit
headSha.description: The commit the changed files were read at. Every figure in this entry is a reading of it.

baseSha.title: Base commit
baseSha.description: The commit of the branch the pull request asks to change, recorded when it was fetched.

files.title: Changed files
files.description: How many changed files were read.

thresholds.title: Chance thresholds
thresholds.description: The threshold each reference's own permutation null sets for this pull request's files, in bits, keyed by the reference's name. A pull request is scored against its own null, never the working tree's: the chance-expected maximum of a few files is not the chance-expected maximum of the tree.

signals.title: Signals
signals.description: The pull request's words and published phrases clearing every one of its thresholds, each stating PULL_REQUEST as its source.

statement.title: What the pull request says
statement.description: The divergence between a reading of the pull request's statement — its title, its description and the messages of its commits, fetched and pinned beside its files — and the reading of its changed files above. The stated words never enter the written reading and the written words never enter the stated one. Absent where no statement was fetched, or where nothing in it could be read. The divergence is a gap, not a verdict: a pull request mixing two concerns states one of them.

sentences.title: Sentences
sentences.description: How many sentences the readable statement carries, after markdown and hidden comments are stripped.

words.title: Words
words.description: How many words those sentences carry. The chance sample matches it: the same sentences, each the same length, filled from the changed files' own written words.

divergenceBits.title: Divergence in bits
divergenceBits.description: The Jensen–Shannon divergence between the stated and written readings, bounded at 1 bit by its own definition.

chanceDivergenceBits.title: Chance divergence in bits
chanceDivergenceBits.description: The divergence the furthest of the statements judged together would reach by chance. A statement whose divergenceBits does not exceed it has shown its own length, not a gap.

chanceRate.title: Chance rate
chanceRate.description: How often chance alone drew a divergence at least this large, in the unit the draw count allows.

resamples.title: Resamples
resamples.description: How many chance statements could be read at all.

topics.title: Topics carrying the distance
topics.description: Which topics account for the divergence and which side each concentrates in, largest term first. Empty where the divergence does not exceed its chance. Only the leading topics are listed, so summing the rows understates the whole.

topic.title: Topic
topic.description: The label the topic resource publishes, in that resource's own spelling.

divergenceBits.title: Term of the divergence in bits
divergenceBits.description: This topic's term of the divergence. The terms across every topic sum to divergenceBits.

statedShare.title: Stated share
statedShare.description: The topic's share of what the statement placed.

writtenShare.title: Written share
writtenShare.description: The topic's share of what the changed files placed.

work.title: The work the pull request states
work.description: What the pull request's work is, against the published change standards and against its own diff. The stated side parses every non-blank line of the authored statement under the Conventional Commits grammar and keeps a type only where the bundled standard states it, so a statement in another style yields counts and no class — abstention stated, never a guess. The written side is the parse's own answer: the changed files at the head commit read against the same files at the base commit, both pinned by the fetch step. No change class is named from the diff, because no bundled standard states one. Absent where the fetch step pinned neither a statement nor a base tree.

issues.title: Issues the statement references
issues.description: The tracker's own statements about the issues the statement references: the repository's pom names its tracker in issueManagement, the fetch step reads each referenced issue of that project from the tracker and pins the answer, and the type here is the tracker's word verbatim, never mapped onto another standard's vocabulary. Absent where the statement references no issue of the repository's own tracker, or the repository states no tracker.

key.title: Key
key.description: The issue key, as the statement writes it.

type.title: Stated type
type.description: The issue type the tracker states, verbatim.

url.title: URL
url.description: The tracker's own page for the issue.

stated.title: Stated class
stated.description: What the statement says its change is, under the Conventional Commits grammar.

linesRead.title: Lines read
linesRead.description: How many non-blank lines of the authored statement were offered to the grammar.

linesParsed.title: Lines the grammar parsed
linesParsed.description: How many of those lines the grammar parsed, whatever their type — a parsed type the standard does not state counts here and in no class.

classes.title: Stated classes
classes.description: The types the standard states, most-written first. Empty where no line states one.

type.title: Type
type.description: The token as the standard writes it — feat, fix, docs.

module.title: Defining source
module.description: Which source defines it, as the bundled resource's own column states: specification, or angular-convention.

lines.title: Lines
lines.description: How many statement lines state it.

written.title: Written class
written.description: What the changed files do to the declarations that stood before them: the pull request's tree at its head read against the same files at its base. Declarations are matched as a multiset on the file, the enclosing declarations, the kind and the name, so two overloads of one name are two declarations and a rename is one removed and one added — nothing is matched across a rename, because the alternative is a similarity heuristic asserting an intention the text does not state.

filesRead.title: Files read
filesRead.description: How many of the pull request's files the reading's own scopes reach, which is fewer than the files it changed wherever it changed a file no scope reads.

filesAdded.title: Files added
filesAdded.description: How many of those files stand at the head and not at the base.

added.title: Declarations added
added.description: The declarations standing at the head that did not stand at the base, counted by what they are in the syntax. A zero is a count: the parse read the files and found none of that kind added.

types.title: Types
types.description: Classes, interfaces, enums, records and annotations.

methods.title: Methods
methods.description: Methods and constructors. A constructor is read here where the vocabulary reading leaves it out, because its name being its type's name is a fact about words and not about declarations.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: Fields, enum constants and record components.

removed.title: Declarations removed
removed.description: The declarations standing at the base that do not stand at the head, counted the same way.

kept.title: Declarations kept
kept.description: How many of the head's declarations stood at the base under the same name in the same enclosing declarations.

filesByKind.title: Files by kind
filesByKind.description: How many of the files the pull request changed are of each kind, accounting for all of them: the kinds the build's own layout states — production, tests, fixtures, documentation, build — and other for a file the build declares nowhere, such as a changelog. The tree's own .readingignore travels with the copy and is counted under no kind.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: production, tests, fixtures, documentation, build, or other.

files.title: Files
files.description: How many of the files read are of that kind.

atHead.title: At the head commit
atHead.description: What the changed files measure as the pull request leaves them.

commentLines.title: Comment lines
commentLines.description: How many lines the authors wrote as javadoc or as comments, each counted at what the parse says one occurrence of it is worth. Prose standing in every file was written once and copied into the rest, so a licence header counts once over the tree rather than once per file.

metrics.title: Size and complexity
metrics.description: The size and complexity of what the files declare. Size is counted in statements and in members, never in lines. The quantiles are the nearest-rank ones, which need no interpolation and land on a figure some method actually has; the largest alone says what the worst method is and nothing about the rest. The complexity is McCabe's (https://doi.org/10.1109/TSE.1976.233837), whose own paper proposes ten as the limit for one module.

name.title: Name

typesAddedWithoutATest.title: Types added with no test
typesAddedWithoutATest.description: The types the change adds to what the build publishes and adds no test for, where a test is a class whose name Maven Surefire's own default includes would run — Test*, *Test, *Tests, *TestCase — and its subject is the name that pattern leaves. Each is named beside the test it arrives without. It says no test arrived with the type, never that nothing covers it: a type may be exercised by a test that already stood.

path.title: File
path.description: The file the declaration stands in, relative to the pull request's own directory.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name, under the declarations it sits inside, written outermost first and separated by dots.

test.title: Test it arrives without
test.description: The class name the first of Surefire's default includes, Test*, gives for a test of this type. The name is read back through the same four patterns, so it is one that build would run. Empty where the type's own name is not one those patterns carry — a name not opening as a type name does.

inferred.title: The word a definition covers the shape with
inferred.description: The Conventional Commits type the measured shape of this change falls under, read from the bundled mapping change-shape-types.tsv. That file states one row per shape the reading can measure, in the order its rules apply, quoting the publisher's own definition beside the measurement so the pairing can be checked — a change that only adds declarations against "a commit of the type feat introduces a new feature". Shapes the mapping states no type for are rows too, each carrying the reason the reading names nothing. Absent where the shape this change has is one of those.

type.title: Token
type.description: The token as the standard writes it.

definition.title: Definition
definition.description: The publisher's own sentence, so the word can be checked against the shape.

shape.title: Shape
shape.description: What was measured that the definition covers, as a clause completing "it …".

repository.title: Repository
repository.description: The repository the pull request is of, as the host names it — owner/name. Absent where the fetch step recorded none.

concepts.title: What published vocabularies call these words
concepts.description: The concepts the vocabularies this repository's own reading published state for terms the changed files write, most written first. Only those vocabularies are asked: a vocabulary the whole-tree reading refused is refused for the tree a pull request joins, and reading a changed file against it would report the accidental matches that reading already measured and threw out. What is here is still a match and never a placement — the bar a placement clears is drawn over a whole tree, and a few changed files are too small a field for it.

term.title: Term
term.description: The words matched, as the files write them.

concept.title: Concept
concept.description: The concept the vocabulary states for them.

definition.title: Definition
definition.description: The publisher's own prose for that concept. Absent where it states none.

occurrences.title: Occurrences
occurrences.description: How often these files write the term.

statedPath.title: Levels above it
statedPath.description: Every level the publisher states above the concept, broadest first, so a reader sees the subject it sits under and not only the concept. Where the publisher states none, the module it files the concept in. Empty where it states neither.

repositoryCode.title: The repository's own code
repositoryCode.description: What the whole working tree measures at the commit it was read at, so a pull request's figures are read against the code they join rather than against a number chosen here. A method carrying sixty statements says one thing where the repository's own worst carries sixty-two and another where it carries two hundred.

signal.title: Signal
signal.description: One word or published phrase written at a higher density than every reference it is scored against, in whichever source readFrom states.

readFrom.title: Source read
readFrom.description: Which source supplied the signal. CLONE is the working tree; PULL_REQUEST is one pull request's changed files at its head commit.

word.title: Word
word.description: The word as the identifier splitter produced it. A run of words a topical resource publishes as one entry is one word here, its words joined by the underscore the resources themselves write: `part_of_speech`.

occurrences.title: Occurrences
occurrences.description: How many times the repository writes it.

occurrencesInNames.title: Occurrences in declared names
occurrencesInNames.description: How many of those occurrences are a declared name rather than prose. `citationSource` contributes to this count; the javadoc above it does not.

divergenceBits.title: Score in bits
divergenceBits.description: This word's term of the Jensen-Shannon divergence between the repository's word distribution and the reference's. Base-2 logarithms bound it at 1 bit. A word the repository writes at the reference's own density scores 0.

marginBits.title: Score at the reference's own error
marginBits.description: The same term computed with the reference's share moved one standard error toward the repository's — the score with the reference's own sampling error held against the word. The verdict rests on it: every signal's margin exceeds every reference's chance threshold, and a word whose score clears the thresholds while its margin does not is counted in `setAside.wordsWithinTheReferencesError` instead of listed here.

closestReference.title: Reference giving the lowest score
closestReference.description: The reference scoring this word lowest, which is the score reported. `get` scores high against ordinary English and low against the Java platform's own API, so the platform is its closest reference.

site.title: File and line
site.description: Where to read the evidence behind a figure.

file.description: The path relative to the root of the repository that was read.

line.description: The line within that file, counting from 1.
